entry.title: Noninteger completely monotonic degrees of Stirling remainders and their derivatives
entry.summary: For Stirling expansions truncated after at least two Bernoulli terms, we disprove the three real-degree conjectures recorded by Mahmoud and Qi for the signed remainders of the logarithm of the gamma function and their derivatives. We give a unified proof of the corresponding integer-degree formula, recovering known cases and resolving Zhu's conjectures for higher derivatives in this range. Every real completely monotonic degree lies strictly between the predicted integer and the next integer. We obtain a universal fractional lower bound through an explicit inverse function and a simpler rational bound valid for every derivative order. A local estimate for the negative part of the Laplace kernel's derivative with respect to its logarithmic variable makes the lower improvement proportional to the reciprocal of the combined truncation and derivative order. Together with a uniform upper bound, this determines the exact order of decay of the fractional excess for each fixed derivative order and for its supremum over all derivative orders. Sharper kernel estimates give stronger bounds for the first two degrees. The proof combines fractional positivity criteria, the classical Laplace representation, a sign characterization of the associated densities, and a convexity obstruction at the upper integer endpoint. All estimates used in the proofs are analytic. The exact real degrees and the optimal asymptotic constants remain open.

entry.title: Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture
entry.summary: We prove the corrected Bessis--Moussa--Villani pinching conjecture for all symmetrized word averages. For Hermitian matrices $A,B$ and $D=E_A(B)$, we construct a positive compactly supported measure $ζ_{A,B}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ such that \[ \Tr f(xA+yB)-\Tr f(xA+yD) =y^2\int_{\mathbb R^2}f''(xa+yb)\,dζ_{A,B}(a,b). \] Its total mass is $\frac12\|B-D\|_2^2$. This representation proves the corrected conjecture, including its equality cases, and gives a positive bivariate moment representation for the coefficient differences. We also derive complete monotonicity of normalized exponential pinching defects and a comparison with Lie--Trotter approximations. A one-dimensional second-order loss measure is obtained for trace-preserving conditional expectations on finite tracial von Neumann algebras. Finally, we relate $ζ_{A,B}$ to Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure by an explicit positive radial transform.

entry.title: The Prevalence of Straight Shots in Control Space for Reaching Optimal Quantum Performance
entry.summary: Gradient-based algorithms are often applied to identify an optimal control for maximizing a quantum objective functional by following a steepest ascent path to the top of the control landscape. In contrast, this paper explores straight shots through control space where movement along such a path corresponds to a less demanding monotonic complete climb up the landscape for the optimal objective value. Existing studies of control landscapes have revealed the presence of straight shots, but identifying them required computationally intensive stochastic methods. In this paper, we introduce a non-stochastic straight-shot search algorithm (STSA) that identifies a large class of straight shots. We apply STSA to numerically generate more than 10,000 distinct straight-shot optimization paths and analyze their statistical distribution for each of the objectives of (i) state-to-state transitions, (ii) general observables, and (iii) unitary transformation generation. The results show a decrease in the nearest-neighbor distances among straight shots as the sample size increases, suggesting their prevalence in control space. We further conjecture that the starting locations of the straight-shot pathways on a landscape level set may form connected neighborhoods, motivating future investigation into their underlying topological structure. The present paper focuses on the use of STSA for locating massive numbers of straight solutions. However, the STSA is not a high-efficiency algorithm in its present form, but the discovered prevalence of control straight shots leaves open future advances to accelerate the discovery of straight shots as optimal controls.

entry.title: Counterexamples to the Monotone Completeness Conjecture
entry.summary: Combining a modification of the recent counterexample to the quasitrace conjecture with model-theoretic reductions due to the first author, we exhibit a counterexample to the monotone completeness conjecture. We fully reproduce the disproof of the quasitrace conjecture by a modified construction and arguments.

entry.title: Rényi multi-entropy of graph states and the $n -> 1$ limit
entry.summary: Rényi multi-entropy extends the Rényi entropy to pure states of more than two parties. It is defined by a replica contraction at integer replica number $n$, and the multi-entropy is its $n\to1$ limit. In holography this limit is conjectured to compute the area of a minimal soap-film web in the bulk. Understanding multi-entropy for general states, however, is harder. Unlike the bipartite case, the replica contraction is not a moment of a density matrix, and the continuation to $n=1$ has to be found by other means. We study this problem for qubit graph states. We show that at every odd $n$ the contraction equals $2^{-k/2}$, where $k$ is a sum of ranks of matrices over a finite field, one row and one column per qubit. We define a class of graphs that we call collision-controlled, for which the rank sum is a polynomial in $n$. This class includes graphs without even cycles and all complete bipartite graphs. The natural polynomial $n \to 1$ continuation is a finite sum over partitions of the parties. While the Rényi multi-entropy is non-increasing under single-qubit Pauli measurements at every odd integer $n>1$, the continuation to $n=1$ is not. A $Z$ measurement on one qubit of an odd ring with $2r + 1 \geq 7$ qubits raises it from $(r+1)\log 2$ to $(2r-1) \log 2$. Thus the continuation is not an entanglement monotone.

entry.title: Lattice Bruhat intervals are polytopal
entry.summary: For a Bruhat interval $[x,y]$ in an arbitrary Coxeter group which is a lattice, we give a type-uniform construction of a convex polytope whose complete face lattice realizes $[x,y]$. This gives a polytopal realization of the coincidence between classical Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials for lattice Bruhat intervals and Stanley's toric $g$-polynomials. Consequently, the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial of a lattice Bruhat interval cannot have internal zeros, satisfies a multiplicative strengthening of monotonicity, and obeys the generalized upper bound theorem for polytopes. For lattice Bruhat intervals in finite Weyl groups, we explain the relation with the toric geometry of Richardson varieties and derive formulas for their local and global intersection cohomology, as well as a Boolean criterion for rational smoothness. We conjecture that the coefficients of these Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials form an $M$-sequence.

entry.title: Model theory of quasitracial $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras and the absoluteness of monotone completeness
entry.summary: We examine various applications of logic to $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras, particularly the monotone completeness conjecture. We develop a model theory for $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras equipped with a faithful normalized quasitrace. Using this language, we provide a separable coding which allows us to reduce the finite case of the monotone completeness conjecture to monotone sequential completeness of $\mathrm{II}_1$ $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factors. Combining an explicit recursive axiomatization with the completeness theorem for continuous logic, we show that this case of the conjecture, and Kaplansky's problem whether every $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factor of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ is a von Neumann algebra, are each equivalent in ZFC to a $Π^0_2$ sentence of arithmetic, so that their answers are the same in every $ω$-model of ZFC. We also consider real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras. Here the Baer-$*$-ring notion of an abelian projection must be distinguished from commutativity; following the real-operator-algebra terminology we call the former semi-abelian. Handelman's matrix theorem implies that a real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebra with no nonzero central semi-abelian projection has $\mathrm{AW}^*$ complexification. We answer a number of other open problems in real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras.

entry.title: Invariant sets and spectral rigidity of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms
entry.summary: We solve a well-known question of Polterovich from 2002 regarding the rigidity of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms in Hofer's metric in dimension two: every non-trivial Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a surface of genus at least one has all positive iterations separated from the identity in Hofer's metric. In higher dimensions, we make progress on the case of autonomous Hamiltonian flows: we prove Hofer non-recurrence for symplectically hyperbolic manifolds, and completely characterize Hofer recurrence for functions of the moment polytope on monotone toric manifolds. These results apply equally well to Viterbo's spectral metric, settling cases of the $γ$-rigidity conjecture, and therefore in many cases also to the $C^0$-metric. Our approach relies on the philosophy that symplectically visible invariant sets govern symplectic non-recurrence phenomena. In dimension two, we use invariant annuli provided by low-dimensional dynamics, and apply methods of $C^0$ symplectic topology to approximately invariant Lagrangian submanifolds. For symplectically hyperbolic manifolds, the invariant sets are provided by sublevel and superlevel sets of autonomous Hamiltonians, while in the toric case, they comprise Lagrangian torus fibers. Across the arguments, we use quantitative Lagrangian Floer theory and its relation to notions of classical dynamics.

entry.title: A complete classification of singularities for radial solutions of the Stefan problem
entry.summary: We investigate singularities of radial solutions of the classical two-phase and one-phase Stefan problem. In a remarkable result, M.A. Herrero and J.J.L. Velazquez show existence of a solution such that the free boundary described by $g(t)$ satisfies in dimension $n\geq 3$ $$g(t)=c_n \sqrt{t} |\log t|^{\frac{-1}{n - 2}} (1 + o(1)), t\to 0,$$ and they conjecture that these asymptotics hold in general. Here we prove the conjecture for all radial solutions, which means complete asymptotic rigidity in that class. In order to obtain these precise asymptotics for the two-phase Stefan problem, for which frequency formulas and monotonicity formulas are unknown, we apply the Potential Reduction to ODE method introduced in arXiv:2608.18913 for the Neumann Bernoulli problem. The philosophy of that method is that the asymptotic shape of the free surface is governed by a precise ordinary differential equation. The fact that we can apply it in this paper to an equation of different type with quasilinear principal part, which is in our regime not the perturbation of a linear operator, confirms the versatility of the method.

entry.title: The Two-Dimensional Majority Rule is P-Complete
entry.summary: We prove that prediction for the synchronous two-dimensional majority rule is $\mathrm{P}$-complete under logspace many-one reductions, resolving a problem open for almost three decades. In 1997, Moore established $\mathrm{P}$-completeness in dimension three and higher and conjectured that the two-dimensional case admits an efficient parallel algorithm. We consider an $n\times n$ torus on which each cell follows the majority of its four nearest neighbors and retains its current state in a tie. Given an explicitly specified initial configuration and a time $T$, prediction asks whether a designated cell is in state $+1$ at time $T$. The central challenge is to make independent information streams cross in the plane under a homogeneous, monotone, diffusive local rule. We overcome this obstacle through a temporal encoding of Boolean values: both values generate activity, but are distinguished by signal arrival times. This encoding yields a crossover that preserves both values and composes with wires, duplication, and AND and OR gates to simulate arbitrary monotone Boolean circuits. Thus a local rule that favors agreement can nevertheless transport, combine, and cross independent information in two dimensions. We also prove $\mathrm{P}$-completeness for deciding whether a designated cell ever reaches $+1$, without a prescribed time horizon. The prediction result extends to every uniform symmetric signed majority rule on the same neighborhood, including the minority rule.
